analysis.title: The Icarus Files: What's next for Nvidia and AI
key_insights: Nvidia rose from 1% of the S&P 500 in December 2022 to 8.5% by May 2026, the fastest rise of the ten companies that have been the largest S&P 500 constituent since 1960. Most prior leaders (GE, GM, Cisco, IBM, AT&T, Altria) fell to a small fraction of their peak share; only Exxon still holds 1%+.

Nvidia's leadership is changing: Jensen Huang is being replaced, and Brad Gerstner (Altimeter) and Gavin Baker (Atreides) wrote to Nvidia's board asking for a process that includes the possible return of Huang. Nvidia now trades at the lowest valuation among large AI stocks by a wide margin.

Microsoft and Apple have avoided the Icarus pattern so far, and Cembalest expects the same for Nvidia in the near term. Nvidia earned 83% of AI chip revenue in 2023-2025 with 75% gross margins and 66% operating margins, trades at a PEG of 0.2x, and has sustained very high free cash flow margins while hyperscaler FCF has eroded on debt-financed capex.

Nvidia holds only 28% of announced frontier lab compute agreements (12.11 GW), versus an 80-90% AI chip revenue share in 2024-2025 per Silicon Analysts. Google TPUs (10 GW), Amazon Trainium (8 GW), AMD (7 GW), Broadcom custom (6 GW) and Cerebras (0.75 GW) make up the rest as shown in the chart.

Epoch AI's inference performance index shows AMD's MI455X at the top per chip, helped by more HBM content and higher memory bandwidth. A frontier lab said onboarding models on AMD GPUs fell from 6-12 months to 3 days using its latest AI model for the engineering, which may erode Nvidia's CUDA switching-cost advantage. Nvidia's Rubin Ultra in 2027 may change this.
SemiAnalysis data on Qwen 3.5 397B shows Google's TPU7x ahead of Nvidia GB300 NVL72 on token output per dollar at all but the slowest speeds.

Chinese open weight models consume the majority of tokens on OpenRouter and are direct or indirect Nvidia customers. SemiAnalysis estimates 1.5 GW of restricted Nvidia chips have ended up in China. The Institute for Progress projects 32% of China's end-2027 AI compute will be remote access to US chips, mostly in Southeast Asia.

The Remote Access Security Act (RASA) passed the House 369-22 and has not had a Senate vote. It would let the US restrict Chinese firms from remotely using restricted chips in overseas data centers and require Asian cloud providers to verify customers and obtain US licenses. If it passes and works, Chinese firms have more incentive to build their own accelerators (Huawei Ascend already cited by Z.AI, DeepSeek and Meituan).

Nvidia under Huang opposed China ring-fencing, and Congressional inquiries may start with Megaspeed, a Singapore company Culper Research identified in May 2026 as funded and controlled by Alibaba. The share of Nvidia revenue billed to Singapore addresses rose from 8% to 22%, and Nvidia stopped breaking out the figure in July 2025.

Over the last three quarters Nvidia spent 58% of operating cash flow on equity investments and M&A. Off-balance-sheet long-term debt and lease liabilities rose from $214 bn to $422 bn between Q1 and Q2 2026, and $530 bn including land, power and shell guarantees. Circular AI-to-AI deals were 26% of AI investment deal value in 2021-2025, and AI-to-AI deals in total were 56%, per BIS.

A shift in Nvidia's vendor financing could hurt neoclouds (CoreWeave, Nebius, Applied Digital, IREN), though their valuations have already fallen this year. Nvidia's supply chain lock on memory and logic wafers may also loosen, benefiting AMD and Broadcom. Yields on AI infrastructure debt (HY and IG) have risen sharply this year and have started to weigh on overall high yield.
Nvidia's support for US open weight models (Reflection, Thinking Machines, Poolside, its own Nemotron) could fade.

Sell-side targets implied a roughly 40% one-year gain before last week. Recent target changes since July 1, 2026: Baird $500 to $200 (-60%), Evercore ISI $413 to $186 (-55%), Bernstein $315 to $200 (-37%), Citi $300 to $225 (-25%), JPMorgan $280 to $215 (-23%), Goldman Sachs $285 to $220 (-23%), Morgan Stanley $288 to $267 (-7%), Wells Fargo $315 to $300 (-5%), UBS $280 to $300 (+7%).

Retail investors bought the 13% decline. Cembalest finds Nvidia interesting for long-term holders at 32% below its all-time high with a 0.2x PEG, and its net debt to EBITDA is still below zero given its cash.

Markers of AI demand still look healthy: rising prices for legacy Nvidia GPUs, rising Taiwanese and South Korean chip/hardware exports, and sub-1% US data center vacancy. Voter revolt in the midterms favored data center restrictions. If that cuts conversion of announced data centers in 2028, Nvidia could benefit as owners upgrade chips to raise token output.

earnings_insights: Nvidia earned 83% of AI chip revenue in 2023-2025 with 75% gross margins and 66% operating margins (period figures cited in the report, not a single quarter's print).
Nvidia fell almost 10% in late February 2026 after reporting Q4 revenues, per the report's retail buying discussion.
Nvidia's net debt to trailing 12-month EBITDA is below zero, meaning cash and marketable securities exceed short and long-term debt.
risk_factors: Nvidia management transition as Jensen Huang steps aside.
Share loss to AMD, Google TPUs, Amazon Trainium and Broadcom custom chips as frontier labs diversify.
RASA or other export restrictions cutting off Chinese models' access to US chips, and Congressional scrutiny of Nvidia's Southeast Asia customers.
Reduced Nvidia vendor financing and investment affecting neoclouds and AI debt markets.
Off-balance-sheet obligations of $422 bn rising to $530 bn with guarantees.
Local data center restrictions slowing new capacity.

tension_points.bull_case: Nvidia has a 0.2x PEG, sustained very high free cash flow margins, net debt/EBITDA below zero, and retail demand on the dip. Microsoft and Apple avoided the Icarus pattern, legacy GPU prices are rising, and data center vacancy is below 1%.
tension_points.bear_case: Leadership change, a 28% share of frontier lab compute agreements, AMD and Google TPUs closing the inference gap, China export scrutiny, and risk of reduced vendor financing to neoclouds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Passage and effective enforcement of the RASA bill cutting Chinese access to US chips, or Nvidia materially reducing vendor financing and backstops to neoclouds.
